_comment: SWEG_STAGING — the faction-neutral threat-range-aware commit heuristic (the closing-side counterpart of the adopted ranged-hold family). An artificial-intelligence piloting heuristic, not a 10e rules claim: it grounds in the core-rules fact that Advancing forfeits the charge (quoted below) and in the universal competitive staging doctrine, and is registered so the citation auditor tracks it. Default-off, byte-identical off.

simulator.staging_discipline.rule_name: Advance move + Charge phase eligibility (10e Core Rules) — threat-range staging piloting heuristic
simulator.staging_discipline.quoted_text: If a unit Advances, then until the end of the turn, that unit cannot shoot or declare a charge. ... A unit cannot be selected to declare a charge if it Advanced or Fell Back this turn.
simulator.staging_discipline.trigger: SWEG_STAGING=1 (default-off; unset is the byte-identical kill-switch); a moving unit with an ENGAGE / CAPTURE / STEAL move intent, not cheap chaff (per strategy._is_chaff_unit), whose would-be sprint destination (a full Normal move plus a full Advance toward its goal) ends inside a significant enemy threat envelope (an enemy of expected damage per activation >= 2.0, envelope radius = enemy Move + max(weapon range, charge reach) capped at 30 inches), that CANNOT accomplish its commit this turn (a melee unit whose nearest enemy is beyond a Normal move plus a charge; an objective claimer that cannot reach the marker even by Advancing; a ranged unit whose nearest enemy is beyond its own range after a Normal move), and for whose binding envelope no friendly mass is committing this turn (friendly expected output already poised inside the envelope at phase start < 0.5 of the local enemy output)
simulator.staging_discipline.effect: ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE PILOTING HEURISTIC — not a 10e rules claim; grounds in the core-rules fact quoted above that Advancing forfeits both shooting and the charge, and in the universal competitive staging doctrine (Stat Check: stage an objective within the enemy's threat range while the unit itself stays outside that threat range, then commit together rather than trickling in piecemeal). The default move logic Advances any unit that cannot reach its goal within a Normal move, so opponents Advance everything into a gunline kill zone on turn 1 and deliver themselves piecemeal (World Eaters Berzerkers Advance forfeiting their charge and die before acting; ~100 Ork units Advance turn 1). When SWEG_STAGING=1 such a wasted commit STAGES instead: the Advance sprint is suppressed (Battle._do_move's shared advance-suppression, the same path as simulator.am_advance_discipline / ck_ranged_hold / votann_ranged_hold) so a melee closer keeps its charge for when it arrives, and for a melee-delivery envelope the Normal move is capped at the bubble edge (Battle._staging_capped_target ray-sphere) so the unit does not walk into an enemy charge it cannot answer. The unit STILL Normal-moves toward its goal every turn (board presence is never surrendered — the officer-front-line -2.19 and screen / gunline-hold rejections that made units passive are the cautionary precedents), so staging delays only the reckless piecemeal ENGAGEMENT over-commit. THREE overrides preserve mission play and coordination: (a) a unit that claims / contests an objective this turn or can charge / shoot this turn commits freely (the fall-back-only-when-wasted precedent); (b) cheap chaff / screens are exempt (screens are supposed to be exposed); (c) when a friendly mass is already poised inside the same envelope (commit_ready, computed once per phase from the phase-start snapshot with no per-activation lookahead), the whole cluster releases and commits together. The threat envelope, commit-mass, and can-act tests are all deterministic geometry over cached expected damage per activation (code.roles.expected_ranged_dpa / expected_melee_dpa); no random draw is made, so the OFF path (gate unset → the per-phase precompute returns None → the _do_move staging block is skipped) reproduces the baseline byte-for-byte. FACTION-NEUTRAL by design (the closing side's counterpart of the gunline-hold family): the envelope radius is CAPPED at 30 inches so a board-wide gun does not blanket the map and freeze every closer — the reproduction of the rejected gunline-hold passivity that cap is built to avoid.
